chunks: What has happened to you, O believers, that when you are asked to set out in the cause of God your feet begin to drag? Do you find the life of the world so pleasing that you forget the life to come? Yet the profit of the life of this world is but meagre as compared to the life to come.

key_terms.اثَّاقَلْتُمْ: you became heavy / you dragged your feet (reluctance)
key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: the Hereafter / the life to come
key_terms.انْفِرُوا: set out / march forth (imperative, often used for military expedition)
key_terms.سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: cause of God / path of God

ai.seo_question: Why were the believers criticized for dragging their feet when called to jihad?
ai.summary: In the context of the Battle of Tabuk, this verse critiques the stagnation of the believers who preferred the comfort of home over the hardship of jihad, a theme deeply explored in Shia exegesis as a test of sincere faith versus nominal belief. It highlights the transient nature of dunya (worldly life) as mere 'qalil' (little) compared to the eternal reward of the akhirah, urging believers to overcome their attachment to material ease. This contrast serves as a spiritual reminder that true success lies in prioritizing the Hereafter, a core tenet in Shia theological reflections on sacrifice and devotion.
